answer.rationale: Daily settlement peak is expected load, so 5x write p99 after a deploy is more consistent with a change-related regression than missing routine headroom. Latency began climbing ~30 minutes after the release, which can fit a staged rollout (memory_b6) rather than a proven capacity cliff. memory_b1 is the closest write-preserving precedent: the prior build was stable and rollback cleared the checkout incident without customer impact. Cause is not proven—peak coincidence remains possible—so this is not a certainty claim. Rejected enable_circuit_breaker because failing fast would drop customer writes (memory_b4) and violates the objective. Rejected add_capacity because memory_b3 was extra headroom for an unusual retail surge, not a normal daily peak on a just-shipped build. No regional signal for failover; replica routing addresses report/read offload, not settlement writes. Flagging downstream settlement-value risk if rollback touches in-flight writes; still the intervention most aligned with sustained availability on known-good code.
